latest_final: The narrator is a married adult who has secretly and deliberately assaulted their spouse — a family member by marriage. This assault is still hidden: nobody has reported it, so it is unknown to the authorities. The spouse, worn down and disappointed for reasons of their own, announces "You've disappointed me so much; I'm never coming back" and leaves the marriage for good. The narrator, watching them go, sighs "Sigh, I know I'm in trouble," because they know that they will be the prime suspect for having harmed the spouse and that the hidden assault they committed can no longer stay buried — it will come to light and they will be arrested and prosecuted for it. In short: a secretly abusive spouse dreads that their unreported assault will be exposed and that they will be blamed and charged for the harm they truly did to their partner.
